goal.en: Talk about the future accurately: decisions, plans, predictions, arrangements and timetables.
goal.ar: أن تتحدث عن المستقبل بدقة: القرارات، والخطط، والتوقعات، والمواعيد المرتّبة، والجداول الثابتة.

text.en: will + base verb, the same for every subject. Short form: I'll, he'll. Negative: won't.
text.ar: will مع الفعل المجرد، ولا تتغير مع الفاعل. والمختصر I'll وhe'll، والنفي won't.

text.en: Use “will” for a decision made at the moment of speaking, for an offer or promise, and for an opinion about the future (I think, probably, maybe).
text.ar: نستخدم will للقرار الذي يُتخذ في لحظة الكلام، وللعرض والوعد، ولإبداء رأي في المستقبل مع I think وprobably وmaybe.

items.en: The phone is ringing. — I'll answer it.
Don't worry, I won't tell anyone.
I think prices will rise next year.
items.ar: أظن أن الأسعار سترتفع العام القادم.

text.en: Never put a second verb marker after will: “I will to go” and “I will going” are wrong. Just: I will go.
text.ar: لا تضع علامة فعل أخرى بعد will. فلا تقل I will to go ولا I will going، بل I will go.

head: Situation
Use
Example
rows: Prediction with evidence you can see
Look at the sky — it's going to rain.
I think it will rain tomorrow.

text.en: Ask yourself one question: did the plan exist before I started speaking? If yes → going to. If it was born in this second → will.
text.ar: اسأل نفسك سؤالاً واحداً: هل كانت الخطة موجودة قبل أن أتكلم؟ إن كانت موجودة فاستخدم going to، وإن وُلدت في هذه اللحظة فاستخدم will.

text.en: Arabic uses «سـ / سوف» for all of these, so the difference has to be learned as an English distinction, not translated.
text.ar: العربية تستخدم «سـ/سوف» في كل هذه الحالات، لذلك لا يمكن الوصول إلى الفرق بالترجمة، بل يُتعلَّم كتمييز إنجليزي خاص.

text.en: Present continuous = a fixed arrangement with another person or place: I'm meeting the doctor at four. Present simple = a timetable: The train leaves at six.
text.ar: المضارع المستمر يعبّر عن موعد مرتّب مع طرف آخر: I'm meeting the doctor at four. والمضارع البسيط يعبّر عن جدول ثابت: The train leaves at six.

items.en: We're flying to Cairo on Sunday. (tickets booked)
items.ar: سنسافر إلى القاهرة الأحد — التذاكر محجوزة.
يبدأ الاجتماع في التاسعة — موعد ثابت في الجدول.

items.en: What are you doing this evening?

text.en: “What are you doing tonight?” asks about arrangements. “What will you do?” sounds like you are asking someone to decide.
text.ar: سؤال What are you doing tonight؟ يسأل عن مواعيد مرتّبة، أما What will you do؟ فيبدو كأنك تطلب منه أن يقرّر الآن.

questions.sentence: That bag looks heavy. I ___ carry it for you.

explanation.en: An offer made at the moment of speaking → will.
explanation.ar: عرض المساعدة يُتخذ في لحظة الكلام، فنستخدم will.

options: She will to travel next week.

explanation.en: No “to” after will: She will travel next week.
explanation.ar: لا نضع to بعد will. الصواب She will travel next week.

questions.sentence: I think the exam ___ be difficult.

explanation.en: “I think” signals an opinion about the future → will.
explanation.ar: عبارة I think تدل على رأي في المستقبل، فنستخدم will.

explanation.en: won't + base verb makes a promise.
explanation.ar: won't مع الفعل المجرد تُستخدم للوعد.

questions.sentence: We ___ move to a bigger flat — we signed the contract yesterday.

explanation.en: The decision existed before the conversation → going to.
explanation.ar: القرار كان موجوداً قبل الحديث، فنستخدم going to.

questions.sentence: — We need milk. — Oh, I ___ get some on my way home.

explanation.en: The decision is made in this second, as a response → will.
explanation.ar: القرار يُتخذ في هذه اللحظة رداً على الكلام، فنستخدم will.

prompt.en: Which sentence shows a prediction based on something you can SEE right now?
prompt.ar: أي جملة تعبّر عن توقّع مبني على دليل تراه الآن؟

options: Watch out — you're going to drop it!
I think you will drop it one day.

explanation.en: Present evidence → going to. Opinion without evidence → will.
explanation.ar: الدليل الحاضر يقتضي going to، أما الرأي المجرد فيقتضي will.

options: I'm going to visit my aunt on Friday.
I will visit my aunt — I decided last week.
Look, the bus is going to leave!

explanation.en: A decision made last week is a plan, so it needs “going to”: I'm going to visit my aunt.
explanation.ar: القرار المتخذ الأسبوع الماضي خطة، فيلزمه going to لا will.

questions.sentence: I can't come on Thursday — I ___ the dentist at five.

explanation.en: A fixed appointment with someone else → present continuous.
explanation.ar: موعد مرتّب مع طرف آخر، فنستخدم المضارع المستمر.

prompt.en: You want to know your friend's plans for tonight. What sounds most natural?
prompt.ar: تريد معرفة خطط صديقك الليلة. ما الأكثر طبيعية؟

options: What are you going to doing tonight?

explanation.en: Asking about existing arrangements uses the present continuous. “What will you do?” asks the person to decide now.
explanation.ar: السؤال عن مواعيد قائمة يستخدم المضارع المستمر، أما What will you do؟ فيطلب منه أن يقرّر الآن.

prompt.en: Match the situation with the right future form.

explanation.en: English chooses the form by how the future was decided, not by how far away it is.
explanation.ar: الإنجليزية تختار الصيغة بحسب طريقة اتخاذ القرار لا بحسب بُعد الزمن.

prompt.en: Make it negative using the short form: “I will tell him.”

questions.answer: What are you going to study at university

explanation.en: Question word + be + subject + going to + base verb.
explanation.ar: أداة السؤال ثم فعل الكون ثم الفاعل ثم going to ثم الفعل المجرد.

questions.sentence: I ___ my brother at the airport tomorrow — his plane ___ at 6 a.m.

explanation.en: A personal arrangement takes the continuous; a flight schedule takes the present simple.
explanation.ar: الموعد الشخصي يأخذ المستمر، وجدول الطيران يأخذ المضارع البسيط.

prompt.en: Which reply is a promise rather than a plan?
prompt.ar: أي رد يعبّر عن وعد لا عن خطة؟

options: I'll pay you back on Friday, I promise.
I'm going to the bank on Friday.
I'm paying the rent on Friday.

explanation.en: “Will” carries promises and offers; the other three describe plans or schedules.
explanation.ar: will تحمل الوعد والعرض، أما البقية فتصف خططاً أو جداول.
